followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability and task-fit.

On capability, Plover leads across the board on the benchmarks that matter for a structured academic explanation — MMLU-Pro (81.2 vs 75.4), GPQA Diamond (64.1 vs 55.6), Arena-Hard (90.6 vs 82.7). Those gaps are well outside run-to-run variance, so for a query that's essentially "explain a knowledge-heavy topic clearly," Plover is the stronger answerer.

On task-fit, I checked whether anything in the query would trigger either model's preference profile. Willet has two strengths I could have leaned on: it prefers warm-toned requests (this one was very friendly) and open-ended generative work. But this query isn't really open-ended invention — it's a request to explain established research-design pitfalls, which is informational rather than creative. And the warmth preference is a *preference*, not a quality effect; the documentation explicitly notes preferences don't correlate with output quality. So routing on Willet's tone preference would mean trading away a real capability advantage for a self-reported comfort signal that doesn't change the answer's quality.

The content is benign, so the harm-aversion dimension that distinguishes the two models never comes into play — that's where Plover's flat preference profile would have mattered, but it's irrelevant here.

Net: capability is the deciding factor and Plover wins it, with nothing on the preference side strong enough to override.
